scenario: Inventory Packer 给你一个 warehouse catalog，要求返回的结果能用 item name 直接查到它所在的 bin id。
scenario_en: In Inventory Packer you get a warehouse catalog and must return a result where an item name looks up the bin id it landed in.
q: Inventory Packer 的题目规则包括哪些？
q_en: Which rules define the Inventory Packer problem?
options: 每个 item 有 weight 和 size
每个 bin 同时有 weight cap 和 size cap
item 不能拆分到多个 bin
输出是 bin id 到 item 列表的唯一格式
options_en: Every item has both a weight and a size.
Every bin enforces a weight cap and a size cap at the same time.
An item cannot be split across multiple bins.
The output must be formatted as bin id mapped to a list of items.
why: 输出要求是 item name 到 bin id 的 assignment。核心约束是两个容量维度同时满足，且物品不可拆。
why_en: The packer assigns indivisible weighted and sized items into bins with two simultaneous capacity limits.

termDefinitions.meaning: weight cap：bin 允许承载的总重量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight cap is the maximum total weight a bin is allowed to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

optionExplanations: 每个 item 都带这两个属性，可行性检查要同时看这两项数值。
bin 有两条独立上限，装箱前必须先确认两条都还有余量。
整份 item 只能进一个 bin，不允许拆成几份分开装。
实际输出按 item 名字对应到它所在的一个 bin id，不是 bin 对应一串 item 列表。
optionExplanations_en: Every item carries both attributes, so the fit check always looks at both numbers.
Each bin enforces two independent limits, so both need headroom before an item goes in.
A whole item goes into exactly one bin; it never gets split across several.
The real output maps each item name to the one bin id holding it, not a bin mapped to a list of items.

scenario: Bin 0 已经放了 Monitor(8kg,6size) 和 Keyboard(2kg,3size)，两者 weight 加起来是 10，正好把这个 bin 的 weight cap 用满；size 只用了 9。
scenario_en: Bin 0 already holds Monitor (8 kg, size 6) and Keyboard (2 kg, size 3). Their total weight is 10, exactly filling the weight cap, while size used is only 9.
q: 为什么这时候 Mouse(1kg,1size) 不能放进同一个 bin？
q_en: Why can Mouse (1 kg, size 1) not go into the same bin now?
options: 它说明这次判断里 size cap 从头到尾都没被逼近过，先不用管它
它说明 Monitor 和 Keyboard 现在应该拆开，分别放进两个不同的 bin
它说明只要一个维度满了，另一维度就算还有空间，也不能再放入新 item
它说明从这一刻起，之后所有物品都必须各自新开一个 bin 才行
options_en: It shows the size cap never came close to its limit in this check, so it can be set aside.
It shows Monitor and Keyboard should now be split apart into two separate bins.
It shows that once either dimension, weight or size, is full, no new item can go in even if the other still has room.
It shows every item from this point on must open its own separate bin.
why: weight 和 size 都是硬约束，任一维度超限都非法。装箱判断必须同时检查两个维度。
why_en: A bin is feasible only when both weight and size limits remain satisfied.

termDefinitions.meaning: weight cap：bin 允许承载的总重量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight cap is the maximum total weight a bin is allowed to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

optionExplanations: size 不是可以忽略的软约束，它和 weight 一样是必须同时满足的硬上限。
两件已放入的商品不需要重新拆分，问题只出在新来的 Mouse 放不进而已。
Bin 0 的 weight 已经封顶，哪怕 size 还剩 1，也照样判定放不下。
只是这一个 bin 满了，其它还没填满的 bin 依然可以正常接收新 item。
optionExplanations_en: The size cap isn't a soft guideline, it is just as hard a limit as weight.
The two items already placed don't need to be split up, the problem is only that Mouse has nowhere to go.
Bin 0's weight is already maxed out, so even one spare size unit doesn't let Mouse in.
Only this one bin is full; other bins that still have room keep accepting new items normally.

q: 填空：找到绝对最少 bin 数的通用 bin packing 是 {{NP-hard}}，所以 Inventory Packer 采用快速 {{heuristic}}。
q_en: Fill in: Finding the absolute minimum bin count for general bin packing is {{NP-hard}}, so Inventory Packer uses a fast {{heuristic}}.
text: 找到绝对最少 bin 数的通用 bin packing 是 {{NP-hard}}，所以 Inventory Packer 采用快速 {{heuristic}}。
why: 题目要的是在测试输入上接近最优且足够快，而不是证明全局最优。贪心启发式是合理选择。
why_en: Because exact bin packing is NP-hard, the practical goal is a fast near-optimal heuristic.

termDefinitions.meaning: NP-hard：还没有已知的多项式时间算法能保证求出精确最优解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NP-hard means no known polynomial-time algorithm is guaranteed to find the exact optimal solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: heuristic（启发式）：为了速度放弃全局最优保证，用经验规则快速给出足够好的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heuristic is a practical rule of thumb that trades a guaranteed optimum for a fast, good-enough answer.

scenario: 你要先写一个简单、正确、速度足够的装箱基线。
scenario_en: You need a simple, correct, fast-enough packing baseline first.
q: First-Fit 的规则是什么？
q_en: What is the First-Fit rule?
options: 对每个 item 都尝试所有已开 bin 的组合，挑出全局最优的分配方案，代价很高
按顺序放进第一个两个容量都够的已开 bin；都放不下才新开一个 bin
把 item 和 bin 都随机打乱，反复重排直到侥幸凑出一个合法分配
不管当前 bin 是否还有空间，每个 item 都直接各自新开一个独立 bin
options_en: Try every combination across all opened bins for each item and pick the globally optimal assignment, at high cost.
Process items in order and place each in the first already-open bin that satisfies both capacity limits; open a new bin only if none fit.
Shuffle items and bins randomly and keep reshuffling, hoping to stumble onto a legal assignment.
Open a brand-new bin for every item regardless of whether an existing bin still has room.
why: First-Fit 是纯贪心：第一个合法位置就提交，不回头。它实现简单且保证约束有效。
why_en: First-Fit greedily places each item into the first existing bin that can hold it.
tradeoff: 先合法即提交的贪心速度 vs 穷举比较求全局最优
whenOtherWins: 如果输入顺序对抗性强，先排序的 First-Fit Decreasing 通常更稳。

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

diagram:
flowchart TD
  Item[Next item] --> Scan[Scan bins in order]
  Scan --> Fit{First fit found?}
  Fit -->|yes| Place[Place and stop]
  Fit -->|no| New[Open new bin]
  New --> Place
optionExplanations: 穷举所有组合能保证全局最优，但当 bin 数变多时开销爆炸，不是这里定义的规则。
First-Fit 就是按输入顺序扫描已开 bin，第一个两项容量都够的就直接放进去。
反复随机重排属于试错式做法，不是这个规则里确定性的一次扫描。
每次都新开 bin 会让 bin 数线性爆炸，完全没有复用已有空间。
optionExplanations_en: Exhaustive search over every combination can guarantee a global optimum, but its cost explodes as bins grow, that isn't what this rule describes.
First-Fit scans already-open bins in input order and places the item in the first one whose weight and size both still fit.
Randomly reshuffling and retrying is trial and error, not this rule's single deterministic pass.
Opening a new bin every time makes bin count blow up linearly and never reuses existing space.

scenario: Bin cap 是 weight 15、size 10；当前 bin 已用 weight 12、size 4，这时来了一个 (w4,s2) 的 item。
scenario_en: Bin caps are weight 15 and size 10; the current bin has used weight 12 and size 4, and then a (weight 4, size 2) item arrives.
q: `b.can_fit(item)` 必须同时验证哪些条件？
q_en: Which conditions must `b.can_fit(item)` check at the same time?
options: item.weight 不超过 bin 剩余 weight
item.size 不超过 bin 剩余 size
item.name 字母序排在 bin id 前面
两个容量条件都通过才可放入
options_en: The item's weight must not exceed the bin's remaining weight capacity.
The item's size must not exceed the bin's remaining size capacity.
The item's name must sort alphabetically before the bin id.
Both capacity conditions must pass before the item can be placed.
why: 两个 cap 任一超限都不能放。正确性测试会抓住只检查一个维度的实现。
why_en: A fit check must require both remaining weight and remaining size to be sufficient.

termDefinitions.meaning: can_fit：判断某个 item 能否放进某个 bin 的可行性检查函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: can_fit is the feasibility check that decides whether an item can be placed into a given bin.

optionExplanations: weight 检查只挡住重量超限的组合，是两项必检里的一项。
size 检查只挡住体积超限的组合，跟 weight 检查是并列的另一项。
item 名字和 bin id 的字母顺序跟能不能放进去没有任何关系。
只写一个维度合格就放行，会漏掉另一维度早已超限的非法组合。
optionExplanations_en: The weight check alone only blocks weight overruns, it's one of two required checks.
The size check blocks size overruns, sitting alongside the weight check as the second requirement.
Alphabetical order between item name and bin id has nothing to do with whether it fits.
Passing only one dimension lets illegal placements through where the other dimension is already over.

scenario: 你在 First-Fit 中找到了第一个能放当前 item 的 bin。
scenario_en: In First-Fit, you have found the first bin that can hold the current item.
q: 为什么 `break` 很关键？
q_en: Why is `break` critical here?
options: 没有 break 的话，后面每个 bin 的 `can_fit` 检查都会被强制跳过，永远判定放不下
break 触发后会自动新开一个 bin，把当前 item 重新放进这个刚开的 bin 里去
break 会让后面所有 bin 的两个容量检查都被跳过，从而让整个放置流程变快
item 已经放置成功，继续扫描可能造成重复放置，或把 assignment 覆盖成错误 bin id
options_en: Without break, the can_fit check on every later bin would be forced to skip and always report infeasible.
Triggering break automatically opens a new bin and re-places the current item into that freshly opened bin.
Break would skip both capacity checks on every remaining bin, making the whole placement loop faster.
The item is already placed; scanning on could double-place it or overwrite the assignment with the wrong bin id.
why: First-Fit 的定义就是第一个能放就停。继续循环既浪费，也可能覆盖记录。
why_en: First-Fit commits to the first feasible bin, so the bin loop must stop after placement.
tradeoff: 第一个可行 bin 立即停止 vs 继续扫描以寻找更优 bin
whenOtherWins: Best-Fit 需要扫描所有可行 bin 后再选剩余空间最小者，那时不能在第一个可行 bin 处 break。

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: can_fit：判断某个 item 能否放进某个 bin 的可行性检查函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: can_fit is the feasibility check that decides whether an item can be placed into a given bin.

termDefinitions.meaning: assignment：从 item name 映射到 bin id 的输出结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The assignment is the output map from item name to the bin id that holds it.

termDefinitions.meaning: break：跳出当前循环的控制语句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: break is the loop-control statement that exits the current loop immediately.

optionExplanations: break 只是跳出循环，并不会让后面 bin 的 can_fit 一律失败，这个因果关系是反的。
break 只是退出当前循环，不会触发任何新开 bin 的动作。
break 省下的是继续扫描的时间，不是让容量检查本身被跳过而变快。
item 已经落袋，继续往后扫会把它错误地又放一次，或把 assignment 覆盖成别的 bin id。
optionExplanations_en: Break just exits the loop, it doesn't make every later bin's can_fit call fail, that causal claim is backwards.
Break only exits the current loop, it never triggers opening a new bin on its own.
What break saves is the time spent scanning further, not the checks becoming faster by being skipped.
The item is already placed, scanning on risks double-placing it or overwriting the assignment with a different bin id.

scenario: First-Fit 扫完所有已有 bin 都放不下，进入 warehouse.new_bin() 分支；测试会校验 assignment 覆盖全部 item。
scenario_en: First-Fit scans every existing bin without a fit and falls into the warehouse.new_bin() branch, while the tests check that the assignment covers every item.
q: First-Fit 的“新开 bin”分支最常见的 bug 是什么？
q_en: What is the most common bug in First-Fit's open-new-bin branch?
options: 新 bin 的 id 一定会被赋成负数，导致后续所有查找都失败
新 bin 一旦创建，就会自动把后面所有剩余物品统统装进去
创建了新 bin，但忘记把 item 放进去，或忘记记录进 assignment
新 bin 不需要遵守任何 weight 或 size 容量限制，随便装
options_en: The new bin's id always ends up negative, breaking every later lookup.
Once created, the new bin automatically absorbs every remaining item that comes after it.
A new bin gets created, but the current item never gets added to it or logged in the assignment.
The new bin does not need to respect any weight or size capacity limit, so anything goes.
why: warehouse 只负责创建空 bin，不会替你放 item。add 和 assignment 两步都不能漏。
why_en: Creating a bin does not place the item; the solver must add it and record the bin id.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: assignment：从 item name 映射到 bin id 的输出结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The assignment is the output map from item name to the bin id that holds it.

optionExplanations: bin id 的赋值逻辑跟正负号无关，这不是新开 bin 分支真正会出的问题。
新 bin 只是一个空容器，不会自动把后面所有物品都吞进去。
只创建了空 bin，却漏掉把当前 item 塞进去、或漏了在 assignment 里记一笔，最容易漏这两步。
新 bin 和已有 bin 一样，也要老老实实遵守 weight 和 size 两条上限。
optionExplanations_en: Bin id assignment has nothing to do with sign, that isn't the real risk in the open-new-bin branch.
A new bin is just an empty container, it doesn't automatically swallow every item that comes after it.
It's easy to create the empty bin but forget to add the item, or forget to log it in the assignment map.
A new bin has to obey the same weight and size caps as any existing bin, no exception.

scenario: warehouse 的 catalog 可能扩到几千个 item，你要判断 First-Fit 的运行时会不会先成为瓶颈。
scenario_en: The warehouse catalog may grow to a few thousand items, and you need to judge whether First-Fit runtime becomes the first bottleneck.
q: First-Fit 装 n 个物品、已开 b 个 bin 时总体复杂度如何描述？
q_en: How should you describe First-Fit's total complexity for n items and b opened bins?
options: O(log n)，因为每次放置都要先做一次二分查找来确定位置
O(n · b)，最坏情况 b = n 时会退化为 O(n²)
O(2ⁿ)，因为要枚举所有可能的子集组合来逐一比较
O(1)，因为每个 item 只放一次，处理完就直接算结束
options_en: O(log n), because each placement first does a binary search to find the spot.
O(n times b), which degrades to O(n squared) in the worst case when b equals n.
O(2 to the n), because it enumerates every possible subset combination to compare.
O(1), because each item is placed exactly once and that counts as finished.
why: 每个 item 最多扫一遍已有 bin，n×b 是 O(n·b)；最坏每个物品都新开 bin 时 b=n，退化成 O(n²)。这说明千级 catalog 下 First-Fit 仍够快，不必换算法。
why_en: First-Fit scans existing bins for each item, so n items times b bins gives O(n·b), which only degrades to O(n squared) when every item opens its own bin.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

optionExplanations: First-Fit 里没有二分查找这一步，它是线性扫描已开的 bin，不是 O(log n)。
每个 item 最多把已开的 b 个 bin 扫一遍，n 个 item 乘 b 次扫描就是这个量级。
枚举子集是穷举搜索的复杂度，First-Fit 从不回头比较，不会跑到指数级。
放一次不代表零开销，扫描已开 bin 找位置本身就要花时间，不是常数。
optionExplanations_en: First-Fit never does a binary search, it linearly scans already-open bins, so it isn't O(log n).
Each item scans at most the b already-open bins once, so n items times b scans lands here.
Enumerating subsets is exhaustive-search complexity; First-Fit never backtracks to compare options.
Placing an item isn't free, scanning open bins to find a spot still costs time, so it isn't constant.

scenario: 评测套件有三组输入：basic catalog、四个相同 item、以及专门打乱顺序来打贪心的 adversarial large catalog。
scenario_en: The suite has three inputs: the basic catalog, four identical items, and an adversarial large catalog ordered specifically to attack a greedy pass.
q: First-Fit 在哪些测试上没问题？
q_en: Which tests does First-Fit handle correctly?
options: 只在空输入上能通过
只在 item 可以被拆分时才能通过
在所有测试上都没问题，包括 adversarial large catalog
在 basic test 和四个相同 item 的 test 上都没问题
options_en: It only passes on an empty input.
It only passes when items are allowed to be split.
It passes every test, including the adversarial large catalog.
It passes both the basic test and the four-identical-item test.
why: First-Fit 正确性没问题，普通输入也能装得可以。失败出现在输入顺序专门对它不利的大 catalog。
why_en: First-Fit is valid and passes simple cases, but it is vulnerable to adversarial item order.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

optionExplanations: 空输入当然能过，但这不是它唯一能过的场景，说得太窄了。
题目从头到尾都不允许拆分 item，这个前提在任何测试里都不成立。
对抗性大 catalog 恰恰是它翻车的地方，说全部测试都没问题不准确。
在普通输入和同质物品这两类测试里，First-Fit 给出的结果都合法且够用。
optionExplanations_en: It does pass on an empty input, but claiming that's the only case it handles is too narrow.
Splitting items is never allowed in this problem, so this premise never actually holds.
The adversarial large catalog is exactly where it stumbles, so claiming every test passes is inaccurate.
On ordinary input and on identical-item input, First-Fit's results stay legal and good enough.

scenario: 评测套件专门设计了一个大 catalog 来暴露 First-Fit 对输入顺序的敏感性。
scenario_en: The test suite includes a large catalog designed to expose First-Fit's sensitivity to input order.
q: 填空：large catalog 有 {{30}} 个 items，bin cap 为 weight {{15}}、size {{10}}。
q_en: Fill in: The large catalog has {{30}} items, with bin caps of weight {{15}} and size {{10}}.
text: large catalog 有 {{30}} 个 items，bin cap 为 weight {{15}}、size {{10}}。
why: 这组数字不是随便定的：前一半 item 先把很多 bin 填到接近满，后一半大 item 因此挤不进去。它是后续分析“为什么 First-Fit 会开 22 个 bin”的输入基线。
why_en: The large catalog is deliberately sized and ordered to expose First-Fit's sensitivity to input order.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

scenario: large catalog 是一个 30 个 item 的对抗性输入：前 15 个 item 的 size 是 4，后 15 个 size 是 6，bin cap 是 weight 15、size 10。
scenario_en: The large catalog is a 30-item adversarial input: the first 15 items have size 4, the last 15 have size 6, and each bin caps weight at 15 and size at 10.
q: large catalog 中 First-Fit 为什么会开很多孤立 size-6 item 的 bin？
q_en: Why does First-Fit open many isolated bins for size-6 items in the large catalog?
options: size-4 两两配对填到 size 8，size-6 一放进去就超过上限
weight cap 才是这里真正的限制，size cap 全程根本就没起作用
size-6 item 天生就不能和任何其它 item 共享同一个 bin，注定孤立
First-Fit 会刻意跳过还有空间的旧 bin，特地去开一个全新的空 bin
options_en: Size-four items pair up to fill bins to size eight, so a size-six item pushes past the cap.
The weight cap is actually the binding limit here, and the size cap never comes into play at all.
Size-six items are inherently unable to share a bin with any other item, doomed to be alone.
First-Fit deliberately skips bins that still have room and opens a brand-new empty bin instead.
why: size 8 + 6 = 14 超过 size cap，早期看似合理的配对留下了无用空隙。后面大物品只能单独开 bin。
why_en: First-Fit packs early size-four items into bins that later cannot accept size-six items.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: weight cap：bin 允许承载的总重量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight cap is the maximum total weight a bin is allowed to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  Small[Size 4 items first] --> Pair[Pairs fill size 8]
  Pair --> Gap[Only size 2 left]
  Big[Later size 6 item] --> NoFit[Cannot fit]
  NoFit --> Alone[New lonely bin]

why_en: Sorting adds O(n log n) on top of the same O(n times b) placement loop, so the worst case still collapses to O(n squared).

Both sort by descending footprint first; BFD picks the feasible bin with the least remaining room, FFD picks the first feasible bin.
BFD ignores both the weight and size capacity limits, while only FFD checks them, BFD skips capacity entirely.
The two are completely equivalent in placement rule, sort order, and implementation complexity, essentially one algorithm.

tradeoff: 更省 bin 数但扫描更多（BFD） vs 更简单但可能多用几个 bin（FFD）

小物品先到会重新堵住后面大物品需要的空间，这正是当初 First-Fit 翻车的顺序。
can_fit 的判断只看容量数值，跟排序方向、item 数量都没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Sort direction doesn't decide which placement rule runs, switching to ascending doesn't auto-convert it into Best-Fit.
Ascending or descending, both are just heuristic orderings, neither guarantees the globally optimal bin count.
Letting small items arrive first can re-block the room large items need later, exactly the order that tripped up First-Fit originally.
can_fit only looks at capacity numbers, it has nothing to do with sort direction or item count.

scenario: 你在 code review 一份 Inventory Packer 提交，测试要求每个 item 恰好落在一个 bin 且 assignment 完整。
scenario_en: You are reviewing an Inventory Packer submission where the tests require each item to land in exactly one bin with a complete assignment.
q: 实现 Inventory Packer 时，哪些是常见的 bug 或风险？
q_en: What are common bugs or risks when implementing Inventory Packer?
options: 放入第一个可行 bin 后忘记 break
新开 bin 后忘记 add item
新开 bin 后忘记记录 item name 到 bin id
对已放入 item 再进行全局最优证明
options_en: Placing an item into the first feasible bin and forgetting to break out of the loop.
Opening a new bin but forgetting to add the item into it.
Opening a new bin but forgetting to record the item name against its bin id.
Trying to prove a global optimum for items that are already placed.
why: 这些都是会让合法 assignment 或记录出错的实现细节。全局最优证明不是本文启发式的目标。
why_en: The common bugs are placement-control and assignment-recording mistakes.

termDefinitions.meaning: break：跳出当前循环的控制语句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: break is the loop-control statement that exits the current loop immediately.

optionExplanations: 忘记 break 会让循环继续跑，item 可能被重复处理或记录出错。
新开 bin 后没把 item 真正 add 进去，bin 的实际内容和记录会对不上。
add 了 item 却没在 assignment 里补上这条映射，输出照样是错的。
FFD 是近似启发式，本来就不打算、也没必要证明拿到的是全局最优。
optionExplanations_en: Forgetting break lets the loop keep running, the item can end up double-handled or wrongly recorded.
Opening a bin without actually adding the item leaves the bin's real contents out of sync with the record.
Adding the item but skipping the assignment entry still leaves the output wrong.
FFD is an approximate heuristic, it was never meant to, and doesn't need to, prove a global optimum.

q: 填空：输出 assignment 的 key 是 {{item.name}}，value 是承载它的 {{bin_id}}。
q_en: Fill in: The output assignment key is {{item.name}}, and the value is the containing {{bin_id}}.
text: 填空：输出 assignment 的 key 是 {{item.name}}，value 是承载它的 {{bin_id}}。
why: warehouse 内部状态和返回 map 都要一致。只把 item 加进 bin 而不记录 assignment 也会失败。
why_en: The returned assignment maps each item name to the id of the bin containing it.

termDefinitions.meaning: assignment：从 item name 映射到 bin id 的输出结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The assignment is the output map from item name to the bin id that holds it.

scenario: 一个 item 太大，不能和当前 bin 的剩余 weight 或 size 同时兼容。
scenario_en: An item is too large to fit within the current bin's remaining weight or size at the same time.
q: 算法应该怎么处理这个 item？
q_en: How should the algorithm handle this item?
options: 临时提高这个 bin 的容量上限来放下它
不能拆分这个 item；继续尝试下一个 bin，如果都放不下就新开一个 bin
把 item 的 weight 放进一个 bin、size 放进另一个 bin
直接丢弃这个放不下的 item
options_en: Temporarily raise this bin's capacity cap to fit the item.
The item cannot be split; keep trying the next bin, and open a new bin if none of them fit.
Put the item's weight in one bin and its size in another bin.
Just drop the item that does not fit.
why: 题目明确 item 不可拆分。启发式只能改变放入哪个 bin，不能改变约束本身。
why_en: Items are indivisible, so the solver must find one feasible bin or open a new one.
tradeoff: 遵守不可拆分约束、只挑 bin vs 违规拆分约束换取放置成功率
whenOtherWins: 如果业务允许拆分装运，问题会变成不同的流量或线性规划模型。
optionExplanations: 临时抬高某个 bin 的上限等于破坏题目定死的容量约束，不是允许的做法。
item 必须整份放进一个 bin；这个不行就试下一个，全都不行才新开一个 bin。
weight 和 size 是同一个 item 的两个属性，不能拆开分别塞进两个 bin。
放不下就丢弃会让部分库存凭空消失，不符合装箱要给出完整分配的要求。
optionExplanations_en: Temporarily raising one bin's cap breaks the capacity limits the problem fixes, that isn't allowed.
The item has to go whole into one bin; try the next bin if this one fails, open a new bin only once none work.
Weight and size are two attributes of the same item, they can't be split into two different bins.
Dropping an item that doesn't fit makes part of the inventory vanish, violating the requirement for a complete assignment.

scenario: basic catalog 是最普通、没有对抗性顺序的输入，用来看 FFD 在日常情况下有没有价值。
scenario_en: The basic catalog is a normal, non-adversarial input used to check whether FFD helps in everyday cases.
q: 填空：basic catalog 有 {{8}} 个 items，First-Fit 用 {{4}} 个 bin，FFD 用 {{3}} 个 bin。
q_en: Fill in: The basic catalog has {{8}} items; First-Fit uses {{4}} bins and FFD uses {{3}} bins.
text: basic catalog 有 {{8}} 个 items，First-Fit 用 {{4}} 个 bin，FFD 用 {{3}} 个 bin。
why: 普通输入下 FFD 也从 4 降到 3——说明排序带来的收益不是只在对抗输入里才有，日常 catalog 也能拿到小幅改善。
why_en: FFD also improves the basic catalog from four bins to three.

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD（First-Fit Decreasing）：先按 footprint 降序排序，再执行 First-Fit 放置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FFD stands for First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit placement.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

scenario: 四个 item 的 weight 和 size 完全一样，这是给排序类启发式设的一个边界测试。
scenario_en: All four items have identical weight and size, making this a boundary test for sorting-based heuristics.
q: 填空：四个相同 item `(7,5)` 测试中，First-Fit 和 FFD 都使用 {{2}} 个 bin。
q_en: Fill in: In the four identical `(7,5)` item test, First-Fit and FFD both use {{2}} bins.
text: 四个相同 item `(7,5)` 测试中，First-Fit 和 FFD 都使用 {{2}} 个 bin。
why: 所有 item footprint 相同，排序不会改变处理顺序的有效信息，两个启发式因此必然打平——验证了“排序只在难易程度有差异时才有用”。
why_en: When all items have the same footprint, sorting provides no advantage.

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD（First-Fit Decreasing）：先按 footprint 降序排序，再执行 First-Fit 放置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FFD stands for First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit placement.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

scenario: 面试收尾时你要把 Inventory Packer 归入算法模式库，方便以后遇到同类装箱题直接复用套路。
scenario_en: At the end of the interview you file Inventory Packer into your pattern library so you can reuse the approach on similar packing questions.
q: Inventory Packer 这道装箱题体现了哪些 greedy/bin-packing 模式？
q_en: Which greedy and bin-packing patterns does Inventory Packer illustrate?
options: First-Fit：第一个可行位置即提交
First-Fit Decreasing：先按 footprint 降序再 First-Fit
Best-Fit Decreasing：可作为更强变体
minimax alpha-beta
options_en: First-Fit: commit to the first feasible position immediately.
First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit.
Best-Fit Decreasing: a stronger variant worth naming.
Minimax alpha-beta pruning.
why: 前三个都是装箱启发式家族。minimax 属于对抗搜索，不是本题主线。
why_en: The relevant pattern family is greedy bin-packing heuristics.

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD：先把 item 按 footprint 降序排序，再运行同一套 First-Fit 放置逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items by descending footprint first and then runs the same First-Fit placement loop.

termDefinitions.meaning: BFD：先按 footprint 降序排序，再把 item 放进剩余空间最少但仍可行的 bin。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Best-Fit Decreasing sorts by descending footprint and places each item into the feasible bin with the least remaining room.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: footprint：本文用 weight + size 估计一个 item 有多难放，值越大越难放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Footprint here is the weight-plus-size estimate of how hard an item is to place; a larger footprint means a harder fit.

termDefinitions.meaning: greedy（贪心算法）：每一步都选当前看起来最好的选项，不回头也不做全局比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step without backtracking or global comparison.

optionExplanations: 第一个可行位置立刻提交，是最基础的贪心装箱模式。
先按 footprint 降序排序，再复用同一套放置循环，是这道题的主力解法。
把 item 放进剩余空间最紧的可行 bin，是比 FFD 更细一步的变体。
minimax 剪枝是对抗性博弈搜索用的技巧，跟这里的装箱启发式不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Committing to the first feasible slot immediately is the most basic greedy packing pattern.
Sorting by descending footprint first, then reusing the same placement loop, is this problem's primary solution.
Placing an item into the tightest feasible bin is one step more refined than FFD.
Minimax pruning is a technique for adversarial game search, a different family from the packing heuristics here.

scenario: 你的贪心算法对输入顺序特别敏感，而且坏顺序会让早期选择堵住后续选择。
scenario_en: Your greedy algorithm is highly sensitive to input order, and a bad order lets early choices block later ones.
q: 从 Inventory Packer 这个案例最该迁移到其他题目的修复动作是什么？
q_en: What repair move from Inventory Packer is most useful to transfer to other problems?
options: 把之前所有的早期选择全部删除重来
不再对任何放置结果做合法性检查
把最终输出结果直接随机打乱
在贪心之前，先按“处理难度”对输入排序
options_en: Delete every earlier greedy choice and start over.
Stop validating the legality of any placement result.
Randomize the final output order.
Sort the input by how hard each item is to place before running the greedy pass.
why: sort-before-greedy 是很多贪心题的关键预处理。它不能保证全局最优，但常能消除对抗性输入顺序。
why_en: Sorting by difficulty before a greedy pass is a common way to reduce order sensitivity.
tradeoff: 排序预处理换顺序鲁棒性 vs 零预处理但对输入顺序敏感
whenOtherWins: 如果贪心选择不受输入顺序影响，排序可能只是额外开销。
optionExplanations: 推倒重来只是重复同一个对顺序敏感的过程，不解决根本问题。
不做合法性检查只会让非法放置蒙混过关，问题不在检查本身。
打乱最终输出顺序不会改变已经做出的放置决定，无助于减少 bin 数。
在贪心开始之前先按处理难度排序，能提前消化对抗性的输入顺序，很多贪心题都能这么迁移。
optionExplanations_en: Starting over just repeats the same order-sensitive process, it doesn't fix the underlying issue.
Skipping legality checks just lets illegal placements slip through, the checks were never the problem.
Shuffling the final output order doesn't change placement decisions already made, it doesn't help reduce bin count.
Sorting by difficulty before the greedy pass absorbs adversarial input order in advance, and this move transfers to many other greedy problems.

scenario: 面试官问经典一维 FFD 的 11/9·OPT+6/9 上界能不能直接搬到 Inventory Packer 的 bin 数分析上。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether the classic one-dimensional FFD bound of 11/9·OPT+6/9 transfers directly to Inventory Packer's bin count.
q: 为什么不能直接把一维 FFD 的近似证明套到 Inventory Packer 这种两维装箱问题上？
q_en: Why can't you directly apply the one-dimensional FFD approximation proof to this two-dimensional Inventory Packer problem?
options: 本文同时有 weight 和 size 两个 cap，排序 key 又是启发式的两者之和
本文其实只有一个容量维度，跟经典一维 bin packing 完全一样，没有第二个约束
本文允许把同一个 item 拆分成几份，分别装进不同的 bin 里去
经典一维 FFD 从一开始就没有被证明过任何近似比上界
options_en: This problem has two caps, weight and size, and its sort key is the heuristic sum of both.
This problem actually has only one capacity dimension, just like classic one-dimensional bin packing, with no second constraint.
This problem allows splitting a single item into pieces placed across different bins.
The classic one-dimensional FFD bound was never proven to have any approximation ratio upper bound at all.
why: 经典证明假设单一容量维度。两维装箱更复杂，sum key 只是实用启发式。
why_en: The classic FFD bound assumes one capacity dimension, while this problem has two.

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD（First-Fit Decreasing）：先按 footprint 降序排序，再执行 First-Fit 放置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FFD stands for First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit placement.

optionExplanations: 这里同时卡着 weight 和 size 两条上限，排序 key 也只是两者相加的启发式，跟经典证明的前提不一样。
这道题明明白白有两条独立容量上限，不是只有一个维度。
题目从头到尾都不允许拆分 item，这个前提在这里不成立。
经典一维 FFD 确实有已证明的近似比上界，只是那个证明不能直接套到两维问题上。
optionExplanations_en: Two caps, weight and size, are both binding here, and the sort key is just their heuristic sum, not the premise the classic proof assumes.
This problem clearly has two independent capacity dimensions, not just one.
Splitting items is never allowed anywhere in this problem, so that premise doesn't hold.
Classic one-dimensional FFD does have a proven approximation bound, it just doesn't carry over directly to two dimensions.

scenario: 你要实现 bin 的可放入判断，避免只检查一个容量维度。
scenario_en: You need to implement the bin fit check without accidentally checking only one capacity dimension.
q: 下面哪种逻辑符合题意？
q_en: Which logic matches the problem requirements?
options: 只要 weight 足够就返回 true，完全不去看 size 够不够
只要 size 足够就返回 true，完全不去看 weight 够不够
剩余 weight 足够，并且剩余 size 也足够，才返回 true
永远返回 true，放完再回头修复超限的 bin 就行
options_en: Return true whenever weight is enough, without ever checking size.
Return true whenever size is enough, without ever checking weight.
Return true only when both remaining weight and remaining size are enough.
Always return true and fix any overfull bins after the fact.
codeSample: return item.weight <= self.remaining_weight and item.size <= self.remaining_size
why: 两个 cap 是同时约束，不是二选一。can_fit 是所有贪心放置的正确性底座。
why_en: The fit predicate must enforce both dimensions before an item is placed.
tradeoff: 同时校验两个维度（正确） vs 只校验一个维度（更快但不合法）
whenOtherWins: 如果业务只有一个容量维度，检查逻辑可以退化为一维 bin packing。
optionExplanations: 只看 weight 够不够会放过 size 已经超限的组合，留下非法装箱。
只看 size 够不够同样会放过 weight 超限的组合，一样不合法。
剩余 weight 和剩余 size 必须同时够用，两条件都通过才真正放得下。
先放后修等于先制造一个非法 bin 再补救，可行性判断必须放在放置之前。
optionExplanations_en: Checking only whether weight fits lets size-overrun combinations slip through, leaving an illegal packing.
Checking only whether size fits equally lets weight-overrun combinations slip through, just as illegal.
Remaining weight and remaining size both have to be enough at once, only when both pass does it actually fit.
Placing first and fixing later means creating an illegal bin on purpose and patching it, feasibility must be decided before placement.

scenario: 四个 item 的 weight 和 size 完全相同，FFD 和 First-Fit 在这组测试上跑出了一样的 bin 数。
scenario_en: Four items have identical weight and size, and FFD and First-Fit end up producing the same bin count on this test.
q: 四个相同 item 测试中，为什么 FFD 不会比 First-Fit 更好？
q_en: Why does FFD not beat First-Fit on the four-identical-item test?
options: FFD 在完全相同的 item 上会被直接禁用，报错退出
所有 item 的 footprint 完全一样，排序没法改变有意义的处理顺序
First-Fit 在这种情况下会自动切换成全局搜索模式
完全相同的 item 不受任何 weight 或 size 容量限制
options_en: FFD gets disabled and errors out on fully identical items.
Every item has the exact same footprint, so sorting cannot change the order in any meaningful way.
First-Fit automatically switches to a global search mode in this case.
Fully identical items are exempt from any weight or size capacity limit.
why: 排序只在不同物品的难放程度有差异时提供信息。同质输入里顺序没有可利用的结构。
why_en: Sorting helps only when items differ in how hard they are to place.

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD（First-Fit Decreasing）：先按 footprint 降序排序，再执行 First-Fit 放置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FFD stands for First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit placement.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: footprint：本文用 weight + size 估计一个 item 有多难放，值越大越难放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Footprint here is the weight-plus-size estimate of how hard an item is to place; a larger footprint means a harder fit.

optionExplanations: 完全相同的 item 不会让 FFD 被禁用报错，排序照样能正常跑完。
所有 item 的 footprint 一模一样，排序换不来任何有意义的处理顺序差异。
First-Fit 不会因为物品相同就临时切换成全局搜索，它还是老老实实按顺序放。
完全相同的物品照样要过 weight 和 size 两条容量检查，没有豁免。
optionExplanations_en: Fully identical items don't disable FFD or make it error out, sorting still runs fine.
Every item has the exact same footprint, so sorting can't produce any meaningfully different processing order.
First-Fit doesn't switch to a global search just because items are identical, it still places them in order.
Identical items still have to pass both the weight and size capacity checks, there's no exemption.

scenario: 面试官问如果 FFD 还不够好，你会怎么继续。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what you would try next if FFD still is not good enough.
q: 最好的回答组合是什么？
q_en: What is the best answer combination?
options: 直接告诉面试官，这个装箱方案已经没有任何办法能再继续改进了，维持现状就好
建议删掉 weight 或 size 两个容量约束中的一个，用简化问题换取更少的 bin 数
建议把一部分 item 随机丢弃掉，用减少物品总数来减少最终的 bin 数目
先提 BFD 作为小幅改进，再提 branch-and-bound/IP 作为精确解
options_en: Just tell the interviewer there is no way to improve this packing further, so it stays as is.
Suggest dropping either the weight or the size constraint to simplify the problem into fewer bins.
Suggest randomly discarding some items so fewer total items means fewer final bins.
Name BFD as a small improvement first, then branch-and-bound or IP as an exact option.
why: 这展示你知道启发式和精确解的边界。BFD 是近似改进，搜索/IP 是精确但更慢的逃生口。
why_en: Naming BFD and exact search options shows the tradeoff between heuristic quality and optimality.
tradeoff: 近似小改进（BFD）先说 vs 精确但慢的搜索（branch-and-bound/IP）留作备选
whenOtherWins: 如果当前 FFD 已满足测试和业务 SLA，继续加复杂度未必值得。

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD（First-Fit Decreasing）：先按 footprint 降序排序，再执行 First-Fit 放置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FFD stands for First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit placement.

termDefinitions.meaning: BFD：先按 footprint 降序排序，再把 item 放进剩余空间最少但仍可行的 bin。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Best-Fit Decreasing sorts by descending footprint and places each item into the feasible bin with the least remaining room.

termDefinitions.meaning: branch-and-bound：通过剪枝系统搜索所有候选分配，找到证明最优的解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound systematically searches candidate assignments while pruning bad branches to prove optimality.

termDefinitions.meaning: IP（整数规划）：把装箱问题写成整数约束的数学规划，交给求解器求精确解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Integer programming formulates the packing problem as integer-constrained equations and hands it to a solver for an exact answer.

optionExplanations: 说死了没有任何改进空间，会让面试官觉得你没有后续方案可谈。
删掉一个容量约束是简化题目本身，不是在优化现有装箱方案。
随机丢物品会丢失库存，跟面试官问的怎么继续改进完全不是一回事。
先说 BFD 这种改动小、平均能再省几个 bin 的方案，再说搜索/整数规划这种小输入精确解备选，层次分明。
optionExplanations_en: Declaring there's no room to improve at all makes it sound like you have no follow-up plan.
Dropping a capacity constraint changes the problem itself, it isn't optimizing the existing packing solution.
Randomly discarding items loses inventory, that's not what the interviewer means by improving further.
Lead with BFD as a low-effort tweak that shaves a few more bins, then search or integer programming as an exact fallback for small inputs.

scenario: 你要把 Inventory Packer 的经验压成几条能带走的规则，用在以后遇到的顺序敏感贪心题上。
scenario_en: You want to compress Inventory Packer into a few takeaway rules you can apply to future order-sensitive greedy problems.
q: Inventory Packer 的主要 takeaways 是哪些？
q_en: What are the main takeaways from Inventory Packer?
options: 先写合法 First-Fit 基线
识别输入顺序导致的贪心失败模式
用降序排序把难放 item 提前
FFD 在两维问题中保证全局最优
options_en: Start with a correct First-Fit baseline.
Recognize the greedy failure mode caused by input order.
Use descending sort to place hard-to-fit items first.
FFD guarantees a globally optimal bin count on this two-dimensional problem.
why: 文章强调合法性、顺序敏感性和排序修复。FFD 是启发式，不是两维全局最优保证。
why_en: The main lesson is to repair order-sensitive greedy packing by placing hard items first.

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD（First-Fit Decreasing）：先按 footprint 降序排序，再执行 First-Fit 放置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FFD stands for First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit placement.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

optionExplanations: 先保证放置合法、能通过基础测试，是后续所有优化的地基。
输入顺序能让同一套贪心规则给出差很多的结果，这个失败模式值得先认出来。
把难放的大物品排到前面处理，用降序排序就能明显缓解顺序敏感的问题。
FFD 只是近似启发式，在两维容量问题上并没有全局最优的保证。
optionExplanations_en: Getting placement legal and passing the basic tests first is the foundation everything else builds on.
The same greedy rule can give very different results depending on input order, worth spotting first.
Processing hard-to-fit large items first through descending sort clearly eases the order-sensitivity problem.
FFD is only an approximate heuristic, it carries no guarantee of a global optimum on this two-capacity problem.
